cards.title: Your first line of Python
cards.body: A program is a list of instructions the computer follows from top to bottom. `print()` is the instruction that shows something on the screen.

cards.title: Text goes in quotes
cards.body: Text in Python is called a string. Wrap it in quotes so Python knows where it starts and ends. Each `print()` starts a new line.
cards.code:
print("I am learning Python")
print("One line at a time")
cards.output:
I am learning Python
One line at a time

cards.title: Every character counts
cards.body: The grader compares your output letter by letter, so capitals, commas and spaces all matter. `Hello` and `hello` are different.

cards.title: Spot the bug
cards.body: This should print three lines, but one of them is broken. Tap it.
cards.code:
print("Hello!")
print("I am learning Python)
print("One line at a time")

bug.fix: The text on line 2 has no closing quote, so Python can't tell where it ends. It needs a `"` before the `)`.

check.question: What does this print?
check.explanation: The quotes only mark where the text starts and ends. They are not printed.

exercise.prompt: Every programmer starts here. Print exactly `Hello, Loophole!`
